sources.mapping: Printed page N corresponds to PDF page N + 1.
sources.coverage: Curated rule summaries, selected spell cards and class progression. Coverage is incomplete. OCR has been checked against the supplied text; visual review is pending.

sources.mapping: Printed page N corresponds to PDF page N + 1.
sources.coverage: Selected additions and options, spell cards and class guidance. Coverage is incomplete. The earlier modified PDF is not used. Errata must be identified separately from this printing.

sources.title: Dungeon Masters Guide
sources.mapping: Printed pages 1–174 correspond to PDF page N + 1. Printed pages 176–238 correspond to PDF page N. Printed page 175 is missing; pages 239 and 240 are unverified end matter. PDF page 239 is unnumbered and PDF page 240 is the back cover.
sources.coverage: Selected combat, advancement and referee procedures. Coverage is incomplete. Missing pages are excluded; tables require visual review before a verified label.

rules.title: Creating a player character
rules.summary: Generate abilities using the method your DM permits, then choose race, class and alignment and record languages, money, equipment and hit points.
bullets: Keep a character record with possessions, spells and cumulative XP.
Race and class eligibility must be checked before choices are finalized.

rules.title: The six ability scores
rules.summary: Strength, intelligence, wisdom, dexterity, constitution and charisma describe different capabilities. The DM chooses the method used to generate them.
bullets: Ability requirements can restrict race or class choices.
Consult each ability's own adjustments rather than applying a universal modifier.

rules.title: Strength and exceptional strength
rules.summary: Strength affects melee accuracy, damage, carrying allowance and forcing obstacles. Fighters with strength 18 roll percentile dice for exceptional strength.
bullets: The exceptional-strength table is restricted to fighters in this PHB rule.
Fighters with strength 16 or higher receive a 10% earned-XP bonus.

rules.title: Intelligence and learning spells
rules.summary: Intelligence limits a magic-user's spell levels and spells known. Learning checks use percentile dice against the applicable chance-to-know entry.
bullets: A successful check determines whether the spell can be learned when found.
The minimum-spells rule permits rechecking failed spells until the minimum is met.
Stop learning in that spell-level group when the maximum is reached.

rules.title: Wisdom: bonus spells and spell failure
rules.summary: Wisdom's clerical bonus spells are cumulative, but become available only when the cleric can already cast that spell level. Low wisdom can cause spell failure.
bullets: The magical-attack adjustment applies to mental attacks involving willpower, not every saving throw.
A failed clerical spell is expended with no effect.

rules.title: Dexterity: surprise, missiles and defense
rules.summary: Dexterity has separate reaction/attacking and defensive adjustments, plus a separate table for thief functions.
bullets: The reaction/attacking adjustment applies to surprise and missile attacks.
Defensive benefits depend on being able to react or dodge; use the applicable combat rules.
Add relevant racial thief adjustments to the ability adjustments.

rules.title: Constitution and hit points
rules.summary: Apply the constitution hit-point adjustment to each hit die; a penalty cannot reduce a die below 1 hit point.
bullets: Under this PHB rule, only fighters, including paladins and rangers, receive constitution bonuses above +2 per die.
System shock and resurrection survival are different percentage checks.

rules.title: Resurrection survival and lifetime limit
rules.summary: The initial constitution score limits the number of times a character can be raised or resurrected. Each revival also reduces constitution by 1.
bullets: Magically improving constitution does not replenish that original lifetime limit.
The resurrection-survival percentage is a separate requirement.

rules.title: Charisma and followers
rules.summary: Charisma determines the maximum number of permanent henchmen and adjusts loyalty and encounter reactions.
bullets: The henchman maximum does not limit ordinary paid servants or mercenary soldiers.
Charisma includes persuasion and personal presence as well as appearance.

rules.title: Race, class eligibility and level limits
rules.summary: The PHB offers dwarf, elf, gnome, half-elf, halfling, half-orc and human characters. Racial tables restrict classes and, for many non-human classes, advancement.
bullets: Your DM may restrict available races for the campaign.
UA provides additional racial choices and revised limits; keep the selected source explicit.

rules.title: Humans changing class
rules.summary: A human may stop advancing in one profession and begin another, subject to ability and alignment requirements. This differs from simultaneous non-human multiclassing.
bullets: Required principal abilities are at least 15 in the original class and 17 in the new class.
Using the former class's functions before surpassing its level forfeits XP for that adventure.
Once the new level exceeds the old, class functions may be combined subject to equipment restrictions.

rules.title: Alignment and class restrictions
rules.summary: Alignment combines attitudes to law and chaos with good and evil. Some classes require a specific alignment or a limited set of alignments.
bullets: A paladin is lawful good; a druid is true neutral under these PHB rules.
Actual behavior can differ from the character's declared alignment.

rules.title: Changing alignment
rules.summary: Voluntary alignment changes can require sacrifices, acts or quests at the DM's discretion. Returning to a discarded alignment is especially difficult.
bullets: The DM tracks the effects of the character's behavior.
Do not treat alignment as a freely changeable label.

rules.title: What hit points represent
rules.summary: Hit points combine physical resilience with skill, luck and supernatural protection. Restoring lost points cannot raise the character beyond their established total.
bullets: Hit-die type and exceptional starting dice depend on class.
Record current and maximum hit points separately.

rules.title: Learning a new language
rules.summary: A character must find a speaker and remain near the instructor. The stated study period is one year, reduced by one month for each intelligence point above 12.
bullets: Study only one new language at a time.
The campaign determines which languages and instructors are available.

rules.title: Coinage and exchange
rules.summary: One gold piece equals 20 silver pieces, 200 copper pieces or 2 electrum pieces. One platinum piece equals 5 gold pieces.
bullets: Coin denominations are assumed to have similar size and weight.
Money changers typically charge 3% for an exchange.

rules.title: Preparing equipment
rules.summary: Plan purchases around both available funds and encumbrance. The campaign may require visiting several sellers, and availability and prices can vary.
bullets: Leave carrying capacity for treasure.
Record where important equipment is carried so it can be reached when needed.

rules.title: Armor class and magical protection
rules.summary: Armor and shields establish a base AC, with dexterity and magic modifying it. Lower numeric armor classes offer better protection.
bullets: Unarmored is AC 10; plate mail with a shield is AC 2 in this table.
Each +1 of magic armor or shield decreases AC by 1.
A monster's AC may represent hide, agility or other defenses rather than worn armor.

rules.title: When a shield protects you
rules.summary: Shield protection assumes the wearer can interpose it against the attack. This PHB rule limits how many attacks it covers in a melee round.
bullets: Small shield: one attack; normal shield: two; large shield: three.
Attacks from the right flank or rear negate the shield benefit.

rules.title: Weapon proficiency and penalties
rules.summary: Class determines starting weapon proficiencies, penalties for using unfamiliar weapons and when additional proficiencies are gained.
bullets: A proficiency covers the magical version of the same weapon type.
Apply the class's non-proficiency penalty to the attack roll.
Check the class table for its additional-proficiency interval.

rules.title: Missile range penalties
rules.summary: The weapon table's armor-class adjustments assume short range. Medium range applies a further −2 and long range a further −5.
bullets: Use the appropriate weapon's listed range bands.
The table also distinguishes rate of fire from individual weapon damage.

rules.title: Hiring workers and guards
rules.summary: Hireling recruitment depends on local availability and the offered wages and benefits. The DM determines local hiring terms.
bullets: Charisma does not cap the number of ordinary hirelings.
Employment can be arranged for different periods by agreement.

rules.title: Henchmen, treasure and loyalty
rules.summary: Henchmen are NPC adventurers supported by a patron. They require upkeep and an appropriate share of treasure, and their loyalty depends on treatment as well as charisma.
bullets: Alignment compatibility matters.
Their XP is usually about half the amount their participation and treasure share would otherwise yield, and can be less.

rules.title: Turns, rounds and segments
rules.summary: A dungeon turn is 10 minutes, a melee round is 1 minute, and a segment is 6 seconds.
bullets: There are 10 rounds per turn and 10 segments per round.
Track elapsed time for light, spells, travel, recovery and upkeep.

rules.title: Range indoors and outdoors
rules.summary: The inch notation generally means 10 feet indoors and 10 yards outdoors for range. Spell areas do not automatically triple outdoors.
bullets: Outdoor range scaling must not be applied to a spell's area of effect.
The source describes special scaled miniature exceptions; use those only in that context.

rules.title: Memorized spells are expended
rules.summary: Casting removes that prepared instance from memory. Multiple copies of the same spell may be prepared within the character's available slots.
bullets: Cross off the cast spell and any expended material components.
Required components must be ready for use.

rules.title: Verbal, somatic and material components
rules.summary: A spell's components impose practical casting requirements. Silence or gagging blocks required speech, and restraints can prevent the required gestures.
bullets: Interruption spoils the spell and removes it from memory.
Check the individual spell for its material requirements.

rules.title: Casting from a scroll
rules.summary: A scroll's spell disappears when read. Scroll casting requires no somatic or material components and normally uses the listed spell casting time.
bullets: This assumes the scroll is already in hand and ready to read.
Scroll effect strength has exceptions; consult the scroll and individual spell rules.

rules.title: Dungeon exploration and mapping
rules.summary: Exploration and map-making slow dungeon travel. Light, probing tools, ropes and a reliable record of the route are practical expedition needs.
bullets: Arrange front and rear protection.
Plan how the group will return and carry recovered treasure.

rules.title: Encumbrance includes bulk
rules.summary: Carrying limits depend on weight and bulk, not weight alone. Heavy loads reduce movement and can worsen reaction or initiative.
bullets: Strength modifies the carrying guidelines.
Ten gold pieces of weight equal one pound in this system.
Consider whether carried equipment is accessible.

rules.title: Dungeon movement rates
rules.summary: During mapping and exploration, each inch of movement rate gives 10 feet per 10-minute turn. Following a known route is five times as fast.
bullets: Flight or combat movement is normally ten times the exploration pace, except for the encumbered case.
Fast pursuit or escape does not permit mapping.
A movement rate of 12 inches corresponds to 120 feet per combat round.

rules.title: Torches and lanterns
rules.summary: The light-source table gives a torch a 40-foot illumination radius and one hour of burning time. An ordinary lantern gives 30 feet and burns for 24 turns per pint of fine oil.
bullets: Track remaining fuel and elapsed turns.
A bullseye lantern projects a narrow, shutterable beam rather than ordinary all-around illumination.

rules.title: Infravision and ordinary light
rules.summary: Infravision distinguishes heat radiation; normal illumination on the viewer or great heat can spoil it.
bullets: Infravision does not provide the light required for mapping.
A thief's body heat needs suitable masking to hide from an infravision observer.

rules.title: Invisible creatures still reveal light
rules.summary: Invisibility does not hide light being carried. Observers can notice the illumination even if they cannot see its bearer or source.
bullets: Different invisibility devices can cover different amounts of equipment.
Check the actual effect used rather than assuming all invisibility works identically.

rules.title: Surprise and lost segments
rules.summary: The ordinary surprise chance is 2 in 6, with special creatures and circumstances modifying it. Surprise grants time before the surprised side can react.
bullets: Each point of effective surprise represents one segment.
Mutual surprise can cancel or reduce the advantage.
Spells still require their full casting time during surprise.

rules.title: Wandering and placed encounters
rules.summary: Wandering encounters occur through encounter checks; placed encounters arise from the DM's keyed locations. Unnecessary time and noise can attract more danger.
bullets: Wandering monsters often offer little treasure compared with the resources spent fighting them.
Negotiation or avoidance can be useful alternatives to combat.

rules.title: Initiative: the PHB overview
rules.summary: The usual initiative check rolls a d6 for each side each round; the higher score normally acts first. Surprise, haste, slow and detailed combat cases can change the sequence.
bullets: Dexterity is not a universal initiative modifier.
Consult DMG combat procedures for ties, multiple attack routines and spell-versus-weapon timing.

rules.title: Saving throws and attack matrices
rules.summary: A saving throw may avoid an effect or reduce its consequences. The required score depends on the saving-throw category, class and level, with relevant adjustments.
bullets: Individual spells specify what a successful save does.
Items can require separate saves against destructive effects.
Attack rolls instead use the applicable attack matrix and target AC.

rules.title: Falling damage: PHB procedure
rules.summary: This PHB passage uses 1d6 damage per 10 feet fallen, to a maximum of 20d6, with surface-related adjustments left to the referee.
bullets: This card reports the supplied PHB text; later interpretations or errata require a separate citation.

rules.title: Encounter and combat sequence
rules.summary: Establish surprise and distance, determine initiative when applicable, then resolve the sides' chosen actions. Repeat distance, initiative and action while the encounter continues.
bullets: Actions may include avoiding contact, parley, missiles, spells, closing, charging or melee.
A minute-long melee round represents maneuvering and unsuccessful attempts as well as scored blows.

rules.title: Tied initiative and damage timing
rules.summary: A tied initiative result normally resolves attacks simultaneously, so both sides can inflict damage. In weapon-versus-weapon melee, compare weapon speed factors instead: the lower factor strikes first.
bullets: A large weapon-speed difference can permit additional attacks under the DMG procedure.
Multiple attack routines and charges have their own ordering rules.
When actions are not simultaneous, incapacitation can prevent an opponent from completing its action.

rules.title: Encounter reaction checks
rules.summary: For a creature capable of conversation, the DM can roll percentile dice and adjust for charisma and applicable loyalty factors to determine its reaction.
bullets: Results range from immediate hostility to enthusiastic acceptance.
Circumstances and the creatures involved still matter; a reaction check is not guaranteed cooperation.

rules.title: Missiles fired into a melee
rules.summary: Missiles aimed into a melee can strike participants on either side. The DM assigns target probabilities using numbers, relative sizes and the situation.
bullets: Determining a potential target is separate from making its attack roll.
The source gives discretion when one opponent group is substantially larger.

rules.title: Casting under attack
rules.summary: Declare the spell before initiative is known. Casting must be continuous and requires concentration; a successful interrupting attack spoils and expends it.
bullets: The caster cannot dodge with a dexterity defense bonus while continuing to cast.
Running, ordinary walking or interrupting the gestures prevents completion.
Completion depends on casting time and the detailed initiative procedure.

rules.title: Turning mixed groups of undead
rules.summary: A cleric normally has one turning attempt, but successful attempts against a mixed group can continue on later rounds against other types until an attempt fails.
bullets: Turning generally proceeds from the lower-hit-die types to higher types.
The DM may apply the stated exception for lesser undead serving an unaffected greater undead.
Turning is subject to initiative.

rules.title: Hard cover against spells
rules.summary: Hard cover can improve applicable saving throws. With at least 90% cover, a successful appropriate save can prevent all damage.
bullets: Apply the actual cover and spell circumstances.
This is a cover rule, not a universal result for every successful save.

rules.title: Morale and losing the will to fight
rules.summary: Morale checks can govern non-leader NPCs, hirelings, henchmen and intelligent opponents. Casualties, lost leadership and superior enemy force can trigger checks.
bullets: Use the appropriate loyalty or monster morale score with its adjustments.
Failure can mean falling back, retreating, panicked flight or surrender.

rules.title: Striking to subdue
rules.summary: For eligible creatures, subduing blows use the nonlethal parts of weapons. Unless a specific rule says otherwise, 75% of subdual damage is temporary and 25% is real.
bullets: This procedure does not apply to player characters.
Eligibility and creature-specific rules still need to be checked.

rules.title: Rest and natural recovery: DMG detail
rules.summary: Complete rest restores 1 hit point per day in the first week. Constitution modifies weekly recovery, and four continuous weeks restore full hit points.
bullets: A negative constitution adjustment removes that many healing days from each week's recovery.
After the first week, add the constitution bonus to each week's healing.
Combat, spellcasting and similar activity do not count as rest.

rules.title: Zero hit points and emergency aid
rules.summary: At 0 hit points a creature becomes unconscious under this DMG procedure, then loses 1 point per following round until death at −10. Immediate aid stops that continuing loss.
bullets: The text optionally allows the triggering blow to leave the creature as low as −3.
After revival: 1d6 turns of coma and at least one week of rest; ordinary cures do not remove the restriction, but heal does.
More severe negative totals can have lasting consequences at the DM's option.

rules.title: XP awards depend on challenge
rules.summary: The DM weighs the challenge against the participating characters' power before determining XP awards. Outwitting guards and overcoming traps can also qualify.
bullets: The award procedure is not simply a fixed reward for every encounter.
Challenge adjustments require referee judgment.

rules.title: Treasure must be recovered for XP
rules.summary: Treasure must be removed from the dungeon or lair and converted to a transportable form or stored safely to count for experience.
bullets: Gold-equivalent treasure can award 1 XP per gp when the challenge warrants it; weaker guardians reduce the ratio.
Items sold before XP is awarded contribute their sale proceeds to treasure taken.
Retained magic items receive their smaller listed XP value rather than sale value.

rules.title: Dividing monster XP
rules.summary: The suggested method divides monster XP equally among surviving participants, with adjustments for challenge and henchman status.
bullets: A genuinely single-handed kill can be credited separately.
A caster protected by allies is not acting single-handedly.

rules.title: XP makes a character eligible to advance
rules.summary: Reaching an XP threshold does not automatically grant the next level. The DM assesses performance and the required period of training or study.
bullets: The assessment ordinarily determines 1–4 weeks of training.
Below name level, standard weekly cost is the current level × 1,500 gp.
Do not treat the next level's benefits as available before training is completed.

rules.title: Mentors, self-training and interruption
rules.summary: Initial training normally requires a tutor of the same class and profession. A performance score below 2 permits self-training at twice the time.
bullets: Name-level self-study and bard contributions have separate rules.
Training must be continuous; serious interruption loses the prior time and payment.
Once eligible to advance, further XP cannot be accumulated until the new level is actually acquired.

rules.title: Comeliness is separate from charisma
rules.summary: UA adds comeliness for physical appearance and initial reactions. Charisma still governs the longer-term interpersonal relationship once a character is known.
bullets: Charisma and race can adjust effective comeliness.
Extreme scores have special effects; consult the full table before applying them.

rules.title: UA weapon specialization
rules.summary: Fighters and rangers can choose weapon specialization at creation. It normally uses two proficiency slots; a non-crossbow bow requires an additional slot.
bullets: Melee specialization gives +1 to hit and +2 damage with the specific weapon type.
Attack rates use the specialization table rather than the ordinary rate where applicable.
Specialization bonuses are not magical and do not bypass immunity to nonmagical weapons.

rules.title: UA double specialization
rules.summary: A fighter or ranger can spend another proficiency choice to double-specialize in the weapon already specialized in, gaining +3 to hit and +3 damage.
bullets: Only qualifying melee weapons can be used.
Pole arms and the two-handed sword are excluded.

rules.title: UA expanded armor classes
rules.summary: UA adds bronze plate, elfin chain, field plate and full plate to the armor table. Field plate is AC 2 and full plate is AC 1 before a shield.
bullets: A shield brings field plate to AC 1 or full plate to AC 0.
Consult the separate construction, fitting and damage-absorption rules for the new armor.

rules.title: Field plate damage absorption
rules.summary: Field plate absorbs 1 point per die of incoming damage until it has absorbed 12 points. Once damaged it absorbs no more and protects one AC worse until repaired.
bullets: Nonmagical field plate must be fitted to its wearer.
Restoring each point of absorption costs 100 gp and one day with a trained armorer.

rules.title: Full plate damage absorption
rules.summary: Full plate absorbs 2 points per damage die, up to 26 total before repair. Damage cannot be reduced below zero.
bullets: After its absorption is exhausted, it protects one AC worse and absorbs no further damage.
Repair costs 200 gp and two days for each absorption point restored.
A nonmagical suit is fitted for one wearer.

rules.title: Bucklers
rules.summary: A buckler protects against one chosen opponent in a melee round and can be strapped to the arm for use by crossbowmen or slingers.
bullets: For a small demi-human such as a gnome or halfling it is treated as a small shield.

rules.title: Apply racial ability adjustments in order
rules.summary: A non-human or part-human character must meet the race's ability minimums. Apply racial bonuses and penalties before enforcing the race's maximum scores.
bullets: Minimums may be met by the initial roll plus the race's permitted bonus.
A score above a racial maximum is reduced to that maximum.
Check the selected printing and UA revisions before finalizing a character.

rules.title: Dwarven resistance to magic and poison
rules.summary: Dwarves gain constitution-based bonuses on saves against rods, staves, wands and spells, and the same bonus against poison.
bullets: The text's examples give constitution 7 a +2 bonus, 14 a +4 bonus and 18 a +5 bonus.
Use the relevant constitution tier; this is not a blanket bonus to every kind of saving throw.

rules.title: Dwarven stonework detection
rules.summary: A dwarf actively inspecting nearby stonework can detect a slope or new construction at 75%, sliding walls at 4 in 6 and stonework traps at 50%.
bullets: The phenomenon must normally be within 10 feet.
Approximate underground depth can be determined at 50%, without the 10-foot restriction.
These facts do not appear automatically: the character must deliberately seek them.

rules.title: Dwarven combat advantages
rules.summary: Dwarves add +1 to melee attacks against half-orcs, goblins, hobgoblins and orcs. Certain much larger enemies suffer −4 on their attacks against the dwarf.
bullets: The larger-enemy list is ogres, trolls, ogre magi, giants and titans.
Do not extend these named racial advantages to every small or large opponent.

rules.title: Elven sleep resistance and weapon accuracy
rules.summary: PHB elves resist sleep and charm spells 90% of the time. If charm passes that resistance, its ordinary saving throw still applies.
bullets: Elves add +1 to attack rolls with a short sword, long sword or any bow other than a crossbow.
The PHB elf is a high elf; UA sub-races can change these traits.

rules.title: Elves and hidden doors
rules.summary: An elf or half-elf passing within 10 feet of a concealed door has a 1-in-6 chance to notice it. Deliberate searching gives better chances.
bullets: An active search finds a secret door on 2 in 6.
An active search finds a concealed door on 3 in 6.
Secret and concealed doors are separate cases in this rule.

rules.title: Elven silent approach and surprise
rules.summary: An elf not wearing metal armor can gain a 4-in-6 surprise chance when alone, with suitable elven or halfling company, or at least 90 feet ahead of a mixed party.
bullets: If a door or other portal must be opened to confront the target, the chance drops to 2 in 6.
Apply the stated party composition, distance and armor conditions rather than treating this as universal surprise.

rules.title: Gnomish magic resistance and combat traits
rules.summary: Gnomes receive constitution-based saving bonuses against rods, staves, wands and spells. Their PHB racial description does not give the dwarven poison bonus.
bullets: In melee, add +1 to hit kobolds or goblins.
Gnolls, bugbears, ogres, trolls, ogre magi, giants and titans suffer −4 on attacks against a gnome.
Do not confuse a saving-throw bonus with a percentage magic-resistance ability.

rules.title: Gnomish underground detection
rules.summary: An actively concentrating gnome can detect a passage slope at 80%, unsafe stonework at 70%, approximate depth at 60% and direction of travel at 50%.
bullets: Slope and unsafe-stonework checks require the area to be within 10 feet.
Approximate underground depth can be checked without the 10-foot restriction.
The ability must be used deliberately; it is not automatic awareness.

rules.title: Half-elven senses and spell resistance
rules.summary: Half-elves have 60-foot infravision and 30% resistance to sleep and charm spells. Charm still allows its normal save if it gets past the racial resistance.
bullets: Their secret- and concealed-door chances match those described for elves.
Only intelligence above 16 adds to their listed starting languages: one at 17 or two at 18.

rules.title: Halfling resistance by constitution
rules.summary: Halflings gain constitution-based bonuses against rods, staves, wands, spells and poisons.
bullets: Halfling infravision varies with ancestry: mixed blood is described as 30 feet, pure stout as 60 feet.
The racial ability adjustment is −1 strength and +1 dexterity.

rules.title: Halfling silent approach
rules.summary: A halfling not in metal armor can surprise on 4 in 6 when alone or sufficiently ahead of an unsuitable mixed party; opening a door reduces this to 2 in 6.
bullets: The stated advance distance is at least 90 feet.
The source's compatible company is halflings or elves not wearing metal armor.
Stout or mixed-stock underground detection also requires concentration.

rules.title: Half-orc ability and language traits
rules.summary: Half-orcs add +1 to initial strength and constitution. Their −2 charisma adjustment applies to non-half-orc NPC henchmen, so retain the unadjusted score for those of their own race.
bullets: Record the unadjusted charisma as well for dealings with half-orcs.
Half-orcs have 60-foot infravision.
In addition to common, alignment language and orcish, they may learn at most two further languages.

rules.title: Humans and racial advancement limits
rules.summary: Humans receive no racial ability bonuses or penalties and have no racial restriction on class choice or maximum level.
bullets: Class ability, alignment and class-specific limits still apply.
The human procedure for changing professions is distinct from non-human simultaneous multiclassing.

rules.title: Multiclass XP continues to be divided
rules.summary: A non-human multiclass character divides earned experience equally among the chosen classes, including a class in which the racial level limit has already been reached.
bullets: Do not redirect the capped class's share to the other class or classes.
Available combinations depend on race.
UA revises some racial choices and limits; choose the source explicitly.

rules.title: Multiclass equipment restrictions
rules.summary: Multiclass equipment permissions are combination-specific. Thief functions retain the thief's armor restrictions even when another class can wear heavier armor.
bullets: The PHB cleric/fighter combinations may use edged weapons.
The source's cleric/thief example uses leather armor and no shield while performing thief functions.
Do not apply human class-change restrictions as though they were simultaneous multiclass rules.

rules.title: Minimum rest before regaining spells
rules.summary: Required complete rest depends on the highest-level spell to be recovered, not on how many spells are missing.
bullets: Spell levels 1–2: 4 hours; 3–4: 6 hours; 5–6: 8 hours; 7–8: 10 hours; 9: 12 hours.
The rule applies to cleric/druid and magic-user/illusionist recovery.
Rest is followed by separate study, prayer or meditation time.

rules.title: Study and prayer time for each spell
rules.summary: After sufficient rest, recovering each spell requires a further quarter hour per spell level in study, prayer or meditation.
bullets: A 1st-level spell takes 15 minutes; a 3rd-level spell takes 45 minutes.
Add the time for every spell recovered.
Count the preliminary rest separately.

rules.title: A magic-user's starting spellbook
rules.summary: The ordinary starting method gives read magic automatically and one spell each from the offensive, defensive and miscellaneous selection groups: four spells total.
bullets: The three selections are normally random, with the table's choice result left to the player.
The DM may allow choices or an extra defensive or miscellaneous spell for an unusually difficult campaign.
Intelligence-based capacity does not automatically grant additional spells to the book.

rules.title: Finding and recording new spells
rules.summary: A magic-user normally finds additional spells in books or scrolls and records those that can be understood. The level-advancement rule adds one spell when a level is actually gained.
bullets: Copying a spell from a scroll destroys that portion of the scroll.
Learning remains subject to the intelligence rules and spells-known limits.
Acquiring a spellbook or a successful learning check is distinct from preparing a spell for casting.

rules.title: Illusionists do not need read magic for their own script
rules.summary: Illusionist books and scrolls use a shared secret language learned during apprenticeship, so read magic is unnecessary for their own profession.
bullets: A starting illusionist normally receives three different randomly determined 1st-level spells.
The DM may allow one or two choices in an unusually difficult campaign.
The later acquisition of magic-user read magic has a different purpose.

rules.title: Clerical spells and standing with the deity
rules.summary: Clerics gain daily spells through prayer and meditation. Access to higher spells depends on maintaining the deity's favor rather than finding a wizard-style spellbook.
bullets: The source distinguishes basic training for 1st–2nd-level spells, divine intermediaries for 3rd–5th and the deity directly for 6th–7th.
Failures of religious conduct can lead to required atonement or restricted access.
Paladin clerical and ranger druidic spell powers follow the stated divine-service principle too.

rules.title: Dungeon rest and encounter checks
rules.summary: A dungeon party should rest at least one turn in six and for a turn after combat or other strenuous activity.
bullets: The referee tracks time for wandering encounters, spell durations and fatigue.
Holing up to rest does not remove the chance of wandering encounters.
Repeated interruptions can prevent spell recovery.

rules.title: Armor encumbrance measures mobility as well as weight
rules.summary: Armor encumbrance accounts for how its weight is distributed and how freely the wearer moves. The listed weights are adjusted game values.
bullets: Bulk and base movement matter alongside the weight figure.
Do not infer identical movement simply because two armor suits have similar weight.
UA supplies expanded armor types and revised details.

rules.title: When the dexterity AC adjustment is lost
rules.summary: Wearing armor does not itself cancel the dexterity AC adjustment. The adjustment is excluded where the character cannot react to the attack or where the specified attack form bypasses it.
bullets: Rear or unseen attacks and giant- or engine-sized missiles are named exclusions.
Magical attacks do not use this adjustment to AC, though applicable saving-throw adjustments can still matter.
Check particular class and effect exceptions separately.

rules.title: Weapon adjustments are against armor type
rules.summary: If the campaign uses weapon-type attack adjustments, compare the weapon with the actual armor type rather than treating every numerically equal AC as identical.
bullets: Unarmored monsters normally receive no weapon-versus-armor adjustment.
A monster's AC may derive from speed, shape or magic rather than worn protection.
The referee may classify natural bony or horny armor case by case.

rules.title: What monthly hireling rates assume
rules.summary: The standard hireling table's monthly rates assume the employer supplies quarters with a bed and other necessities.
bullets: Some skilled occupations add 10% of the normal price of items they make.
Availability depends on settlement size and the appropriate local trade area.
Mercenary soldiers belong to the separate expert-hireling treatment.

rules.title: Porters, pack handlers and teamsters
rules.summary: An ordinary bearer or porter can carry up to 50 pounds individually, or twice that with an appropriate pole, litter or similar carrying device.
bullets: Pack handlers manage loading and handling beasts of burden.
Teamsters drive, load and unload vehicles and handle their particular type of draft animal.
A light bearer is a separate hireling role.

rules.title: Duergar player-character defenses
rules.summary: UA gray dwarves keep dwarven magic-save bonuses and are unaffected by illusions, paralysis and poisons of magical or alchemical origin.
bullets: Against natural poison they use the dwarven constitution-based save bonus.
They do not gain the surface dwarves' attack bonus against orcs, goblins, hobgoblins and half-orcs.
Their surprise and light-sensitivity rules are separate from these defenses.

rules.title: Duergar light sensitivity
rules.summary: Daylight and continual light negate duergar's enhanced surprise, reduce effective dexterity by 2, impose −2 on attacks and give opponents +2 on saves against their attacks.
bullets: Attacking illuminated opponents from darkness instead imposes −1 to hit and gives targets +1 on those saves.
Ordinary torches, lanterns, magic weapons, light and faerie fire are explicitly too dim to cause this penalty.
Drow use this same light-sensitivity treatment.

rules.title: Drow PCs differ from drow NPCs
rules.summary: A UA drow adventurer does not inherit the NPC's 50% magic resistance or automatic access to underworld armor, weapons and poisons.
bullets: The PC retains elven sleep/charm resistance and gains +2 on saves against magical effects.
Drow do not receive the surface elves' sword and bow attack bonuses.
Two readily one-handed weapons may be used without penalty and without a shield; a spiked buckler may serve as one weapon.

rules.title: Drow innate daily magic
rules.summary: Drow can use dancing lights, faerie fire and darkness, 5-foot radius once each per day. Reaching 4th level in any class adds further daily powers.
bullets: At 4th level: detect magic, know alignment and levitate, once each per day.
Females of 4th level or above also gain the listed clairvoyance, detect lie or its reverse, suggestion and dispel magic uses.
These innate uses are distinct from memorized class spells.

rules.title: Deep gnome PCs: defenses and limitations
rules.summary: A player-character svirfneblin lacks the NPC's innate magic resistance and automatic AC improvement, but has +2 saves against poison and +3 on other saves.
bullets: The character is immune to illusions and phantasms.
Once-daily blindness, blur and change self use the highest class level; personal non-detection also applies.
PC deep gnomes do not have psionic abilities under this source.

rules.title: Gray, wood and wild elf distinctions
rules.summary: UA elven sub-races retain many high-elf traits but add specific changes. Gray elves gain +1 intelligence, potentially reaching 19.
bullets: Wood elves gain +1 initial strength and −1 intelligence; strength still tops out at 18.
Wild elves gain +2 initial strength to a maximum of 18 and have sharply restricted class choices.
Use the individual sub-race text and table rather than combining every elven benefit.

rules.title: Half-elven ancestry under UA
rules.summary: Half-elves of gray, wood or valley ancestry use traits similar to the PHB half-elf. Drow-descended half-elves inherit light sensitivity without the special advantages of full drow.
bullets: The source does not provide a half-grugach option.
UA's class and level tables must be checked separately from ancestry descriptions.

rules.title: Racial reactions are directional
rules.summary: Read a UA racial-preference row as that race's attitude toward the column's race. A relationship need not be reciprocal.
bullets: The legend distinguishes preference, goodwill, tolerance, neutrality, antipathy and hatred.
For elves reacting to a half-elf, use the more negative of the half-elf reaction or the reaction to the elven ancestor's race.
These are encounter and social-context guidelines, not automatic decisions for every individual.

rules.title: Ability generation: arrange the best scores
rules.summary: The DMG offers several alternatives to straight 3d6 ability generation; the DM selects the campaign's method.
bullets: Method I: roll 4d6 for each ability score, discard the lowest die, then arrange the six scores.
Method II: roll 3d6 twelve times, keep the highest six totals, then arrange them.

rules.title: Ability generation: keep abilities in order
rules.summary: Methods III and IV retain the normal ability order rather than letting a player freely rearrange scores.
bullets: Method III: for each of Strength, Intelligence, Wisdom, Dexterity, Constitution and Charisma, roll 3d6 six times and keep that ability's highest total.
Method IV: generate twelve complete, ordered sets of six scores with 3d6; select one entire set.

rules.title: Secondary skills are an optional background tool
rules.summary: A campaign may assign a secondary trade or craft randomly or from a character's background. The skill represents limited practical knowledge, with its reach judged by the DM.
bullets: For example, an armorer background can support evaluating ordinary armor or making minor repairs.
This procedure does not supply a universal proficiency-check system.

rules.title: Starting age depends on race and class
rules.summary: Use the starting-age table for the character's race and class, including its listed random addition.
bullets: For a multiclass character, select the class column producing the highest age.
Multiclass age uses that column's maximum possible addition instead of rolling the variable.

rules.title: Wilderness encounters depend on population and terrain
rules.summary: The outdoor procedure varies both the encounter die and the times of day at which it is checked.
bullets: An encounter occurs on 1: use d20 in densely populated country, d12 in moderately to sparsely populated or patrolled areas, and d10 in wilderness.
The terrain schedule determines which of the six daily periods receive checks; it is not automatically six checks everywhere.

rules.title: Outdoor encounter distance changes with surprise and cover
rules.summary: The ordinary outdoor encounter distance is 6d4 inches on the outdoor scale, before surprise and terrain reductions.
bullets: When surprise occurs, subtract the surprise die's indicated value from the distance total.
Scrub, forest and marsh reduce the contributing dice according to their terrain rules; intervening features can shorten distance further.
A distance of one inch or less produces an immediate confrontation.

rules.title: Check for getting lost before the day's movement
rules.summary: An unguided party can become lost when it lacks a well-defined route or a correct map. The terrain-based check occurs before daily travel.
bullets: Following a river, road or similar clear course avoids this particular lost-party procedure.
A correct map prevents getting lost under this procedure; mapped landmarks can reveal an error and permit backtracking.

rules.title: Forced marches exchange extra distance for mandatory rest
rules.summary: A party may raise its daily movement in 10% increments, up to double its normal distance, using the DMG forced-movement procedure.
bullets: Mandatory rest begins when accumulated extra movement reaches 100%, or when the party stops forcing its pace, whichever comes first.
The rest requirement increases with the total extra percentage; use the printed brackets rather than assuming one ordinary night's rest always suffices.

rules.title: Daily foot travel depends on burden and terrain
rules.summary: The overland table measures miles per day and reduces travel for both heavier loads and rougher ground.
bullets: On normal terrain its light, average and heavy burden columns give 30, 20 and 10 miles per day.
For rugged terrain those rates become 20, 10 and 5; for very rugged terrain, 10, 5 and 2.
Burden categories must account for the character's race and strength; the table is not one universal weight limit.

rules.title: Convert flight speed for long journeys
rules.summary: For long-distance travel on a flying carpet or similar magical device, every 3 inches of speed corresponds to one mile per hour.
bullets: The example of a 30-inch flying broom yields 10 miles per hour.
This conversion does not remove a living mount's fatigue, rest or training requirements.

rules.title: Flying mounts need scheduled rest
rules.summary: A flying mount must rest for one hour after every three hours in flight, with no more than nine flight hours in a day.
bullets: A mount also needs suitable training and care; owning a flying creature is not the same as having a trained riding mount.
The daily limit for mounts should not be inferred from the separate flying-broom travel example.

rules.title: Climbing, diving and aerial attacks
rules.summary: The general aerial rules make a climb half-speed and a dive double-speed, with maneuverability-class exceptions.
bullets: A diving physical attack inflicts double damage against an opponent that is not also diving.
Against a ground target, the qualifying dive begins at least 30 feet above it.
Use the maneuverability rules for turns and climb angles rather than treating every flyer alike.

rules.title: Shooting while flying requires practice
rules.summary: Missile attacks from moving flying mounts, brooms or wings of flying use special range penalties and require substantial practice.
bullets: Short range uses the medium-range penalty, −2; medium range uses the long-range penalty, −5; long-range shots miss.
An unpracticed rider using those means cannot hit under this procedure.
A caster hovering with fly or a rider on a hovering flying carpet does not suffer these movement penalties; levitation has separate rules.

rules.title: Wing damage can force a landing or a fall
rules.summary: The aerial damage procedure ties continued flight to how much damage a winged creature has taken.
bullets: More than 50% damage prevents maintaining flight and requires landing; more than 75% prevents a controlled descent.
For this flight check, feathered-wing creatures receive an extra allowance equal to half their normal hit points.
That allowance does not add real hit points or prevent death.

rules.title: Rowing speed has endurance limits
rules.summary: The crew exhausts after 8–10 hours of normal rowing, or after 30 minutes at maximum rowing speed.
bullets: The maximum vessel speeds are burst rates, not sustainable daily travel rates.
Account for crew rest when planning a voyage or chase.

rules.title: Hull damage determines when a vessel needs repairs
rules.summary: A vessel's hull value measures the damage it can take before sinking. Repairs become necessary when damage reaches one-third of that value.
bullets: Damage from one-third through one-half of hull value can be repaired at sea.
Damage beyond one-half requires reaching port for repairs.

rules.title: Grappling prepares ships for boarding
rules.summary: Ships can use grapnels and lines to draw alongside for boarding, while the defending crew can try to cut them free.
bullets: The boarded crew has a 25% chance to remove a grapnel or its line under this procedure.
A galley's lower deck puts its boarders at −1 and the higher merchant-ship or warship defenders at +1.

rules.title: Metal armor prevents ordinary swimming
rules.summary: A character in ordinary metal armor cannot swim. Magical armor is an exception, but its wearer is still encumbered and limited in swimming.
bullets: Carried weight adds drowning risk even when armor permits swimming.
Resolve armor and gear before entering deep water; breathing underwater alone does not make a heavily loaded character buoyant.

rules.title: Track underwater breathing and the return journey
rules.summary: Underwater exploration first requires a reliable way to breathe, such as an appropriate spell, potion or magic item.
bullets: Most such methods last for a limited time, so keep elapsed time and the return route.
Breathing, swimming, seeing and fighting underwater are separate problems.

rules.title: Underwater movement normally uses the dungeon scale
rules.summary: Swimming movement uses the dungeon distance scale, whether traveling horizontally or vertically.
bullets: Free action permits movement at the wilderness distance scale, three times the dungeon distance.
Armor, load and the particular means of locomotion still matter; water breathing by itself grants no swimming speed.

rules.title: Water clarity limits sight
rules.summary: The basic underwater sight limits are 50 feet in fresh water and 100 feet in salt water, adjusted for available light, depth and obstructions.
bullets: Seaweed, fish and stirred sediment can obscure or completely block the view.
Combat on a muddy bottom can leave vision blocked while the motion continues and for 7–12 rounds afterward, unless a current clears it.

rules.title: Thrusting weapons work best underwater
rules.summary: Water resistance prevents effective ordinary use of crushing and cleaving weapons; thrusting weapons remain useful.
bullets: Aquatic opponents normally strike before land-born combatants unless the latter have a significantly longer weapon.
Free action removes this reaction disadvantage and permits ordinary weapon use.
An underwater combat net requires special training; an untrained character attacks with it at −4.

rules.title: Lightning bolt spreads into a sphere underwater
rules.summary: Underwater, lightning bolt changes from a stroke to a sphere with a two-inch radius on the dungeon scale.
bullets: Center the sphere on the point from which the bolt would normally originate.
Everyone in that sphere is affected; a successful saving throw halves damage.

rules.title: Infravision reads heat contrast
rules.summary: Ordinary infravision distinguishes temperature differences; objects at the same temperature can blend together.
bullets: A heat-producing light source interferes with normal infravision.
Readjusting after ordinary vision takes at least two segments.
A sufficiently warm creature can leave thermal footprints detectable for two rounds.

rules.title: Ultravision needs ultraviolet illumination
rules.summary: Ultravision helps outdoors under appropriate sky conditions, but it does not supply its own light underground.
bullets: Underground use requires an ultraviolet source.
Ordinary light, including light from a magic weapon, interferes with its use.

rules.title: Invisibility leaves sound, scent and physical clues
rules.summary: An invisible creature is still audible, has an odor, leaves tracks and disturbs its surroundings.
bullets: Opening doors, disturbing dust and similar actions can reveal its presence or position.
Allies also need a way to perceive the invisible creature; friendship does not make it visible.

rules.title: A charge changes movement, defense and first strike
rules.summary: Indoors, an unencumbered creature charges at double base speed. Outdoors, a biped adds one-third of base speed and a quadruped adds one-half.
bullets: To strike that round, finish within 10 feet. At contact, longer weapon or reach determines first strike; a surviving charger gains +2 to hit.
The charger loses its dexterity AC bonus. With no such bonus its AC worsens by one, except a creature already at AC 10.
Only one charge is allowed per turn, with nine intervening rounds before another.

rules.title: Brace a suitable weapon against a charge
rules.summary: A suitable piercing pole weapon can be set by bracing its butt against an unyielding surface.
bullets: A hit against an opponent charging, leaping or pouncing onto it deals double the normal damage result.
The braced weapon strikes before the oncoming attack routine.
Double the damage roll; this is not an instruction to roll two independent weapon dice.

rules.title: Weapon speed matters for tied melee attacks
rules.summary: When melee opponents tie initiative and both use weapons, the lower weapon speed factor strikes first.
bullets: Large speed-factor differences can permit additional attacks under the printed procedure.
Speed factor is not used to order the initial closing or charging round.
Casting against an attacking weapon uses a separate timing comparison; do not apply one blanket speed-factor bonus to every initiative roll.

rules.title: Dungeon pursuit tracks distance, speed and lost contact
rules.summary: Resolve a dungeon chase by comparing the slowest pursued member with the fastest pursuer and tracking their positions.
bullets: The procedure divides a round into three movement phases; closing to 10 feet produces confrontation.
The distance and time needed to end pursuit depend on relative speed and whether the quarry is visible.
Special tracking senses can defeat ordinary attempts to escape; mapping and measured navigation are not available while fleeing.

rules.title: Distractions can break pursuit
rules.summary: Barriers, dropped food or treasure, and branching passages can interrupt a chase, depending on the pursuers' motives and senses.
bullets: Food and treasure are not automatic escape buttons; use the pursuer's intelligence and interests.
At a three-way choice without sight, sound or scent clues, a pursuer has a two-in-three chance of taking the wrong way.

rules.title: Outdoor evasion depends on surprise and terrain
rules.summary: The outdoor evasion procedure starts from an 80% chance, modified by relative speed, terrain, group size and light.
bullets: A party that surprises the monsters can automatically evade; a surprised party cannot evade at that encounter.
Continued pursuit can require new checks each hour.
A faster pursuing group can close within an hour, producing confrontation.

rules.title: Flank and rear attacks remove defenses
rules.summary: Flank attacks negate the defender's shield AC benefit. Rear-flank attacks also remove the dexterity AC bonus.
bullets: An attack directly from the rear gains +2 to hit and ignores both shield and dexterity AC benefits.
Stunned, prone or motionless opponents are attacked on that rear-attack basis, with +4 to hit instead of +2.

rules.title: Magical sleep and holding create special vulnerability
rules.summary: When the attacker remains exposed to enemy actions in general melee, weapon attacks that can affect a magically sleeping or held opponent hit automatically for maximum damage, with twice the usual attack routines.
bullets: Outside general melee, one such helpless creature can be bound or killed per round.
These special provisions do not automatically apply to an ordinarily sleeping creature.

rules.title: Two weapons trade accuracy for another attack
rules.summary: A character normally fighting with one weapon may use a dagger or hand axe in the other hand. The baseline penalties are −2 with the primary weapon and −4 with the secondary.
bullets: Dexterity above 15 reduces the penalties: at 16 they are −1/−3, at 17 0/−2, and at 18 0/−1, listed primary/secondary.
Dexterity below 6 adds the relevant reaction/attacking penalties to each attack.
The second weapon does not provide a shield or parrying defense.

rules.title: Breaking off melee exposes the departing combatant
rules.summary: A combatant breaking off melee grants the opponent a free attack or attack routine before making the full move away.
bullets: Resolve that attack as against a stunned rear target: +4 to hit with no shield or dexterity AC benefit.
Plan a retreat with this exposure in mind rather than treating departure as ordinary safe movement.

rules.title: Count the actions needed to use gear
rules.summary: At the start of a round, players should state what their characters are attempting precisely enough to resolve timing.
bullets: Retrieving an item, moving and using it can be separate actions; a sequence may take more than one round.
A changed plan starts from the character's current position and progress, rather than resetting the round.

rules.title: Choose the correct saving-throw category
rules.summary: The character matrix separates poison/death/paralysis, petrification/polymorph, rod/staff/wand, breath weapons and spells.
bullets: Read category exceptions: a polymorph wand uses the rod/staff/wand column rather than the general polymorph column.
The breath-weapon column excludes attacks causing petrification or polymorph; the general spell column excludes effects assigned another save type.
The numerical class-and-level matrix remains a source-table reference pending visual verification.

rules.title: A natural 1 fails a character saving throw
rules.summary: The DMG character saving-throw matrix explicitly makes an unmodified die roll of 1 a failure.
bullets: Magical protections, spells and other adjustments do not override this rule.
Use the applicable class, level and attack category for the required score.

rules.title: Multiclass saves use the best applicable class
rules.summary: Multiclass characters, characters with two classes, and bards compare their classes' saving throws and use the most favorable result for the attack type.
bullets: Check each possessed class at its own level.
A single class is not necessarily best for every saving-throw category.

rules.title: Items save according to material, exposure and magic
rules.summary: An item saving throw applies when the object is actually exposed to the attack. Use the material row and the specific attack form in the item matrix.
bullets: Magical items gain +2, plus another +1 for each enchantment plus above +1; a +2 item therefore gets +3.
An item gains +5 against attacks in its own mode, such as fire against a ring of fire resistance.
Normal fire, magical fire, fireball and electrical attack forms have distinct columns; do not substitute one general damage save.

rules.title: An item's fall save depends on height and landing surface
rules.summary: The item fall-save column assumes a five-foot fall onto a hard, stone-like surface.
bullets: Subtract 1 from the save roll for every additional five feet.
A wood-like landing surface gives +1; a fleshy soft surface gives +5.
Use the object's material row for the target score rather than a creature's saving throw.

rules.title: Many rods, staves and wands need a command word
rules.summary: Using a rod, staff or wand usually requires learning its proper command word.
bullets: Clues can come from observing the former owner, questioning them or finding their written notes.
When those sources are unavailable, information-gathering magic may be needed; finding the item does not itself reveal the word.

rules.title: Drinking a potion includes a delay before its effect
rules.summary: Opening and drinking a ready potion takes one segment; its full effect normally follows after d4+1 segments.
bullets: Retrieving the potion adds time before it can be opened and drunk.
For an oil, opening and pouring takes one segment and applying it takes another 2–5 segments.

rules.title: Overlapping potions can interact unpredictably
rules.summary: Check the potion-miscibility procedure when potions are physically mixed or when someone drinks another potion while a previous one is still active.
bullets: The DM makes the compatibility check secretly.
Possible outcomes range from cancellation or reduced efficacy to dangerous reactions; do not assume different potions stack safely.
The outcome table remains a source reference rather than a visually unverified transcription.

rules.title: Energy drain removes the benefits of a level
rules.summary: Losing an experience level removes the hit points gained at that level, including its constitution bonus, and the abilities that came with it.
bullets: Set experience points to the midpoint of the next lower level.
For multiclass characters, drain the highest class level first; tied levels use the class requiring the most XP.
Recording hit-point gains by level makes later drain and restoration easier to resolve.

rules.title: A treasure map is a lead, not a guaranteed recovery
rules.summary: A map can identify a treasure location without promising an unguarded cache or an accurate inventory.
bullets: The route and the destination can still contain hazards.
Treasure abandoned for later collection can be stolen; the DM considers how well it was concealed or protected.

rules.title: Keeping and selling magic items use different XP values
rules.summary: The magic-item tables distinguish suggested XP for retaining an item from its usual gold-piece sale value.
bullets: When an item is sold, base its XP award on the selling price rather than its retained-item XP value.
Selling to another player character still counts as retaining it for this purpose and uses the lower item XP value.

rules.title: Spell scroll XP depends on who can use it
rules.summary: A spell scroll grants 100 XP per spell level only to a character able to use its spells. Protection scrolls instead use their listed XP values.
bullets: The ordinary open-market sale value of a spell scroll is three times its XP value.
A protection scroll sells for five times its XP value.
Do not apply the spell-level formula to every kind of scroll.

rules.title: An observed spell-user may detect scrying
rules.summary: A spell-user being magically observed may check for detection each round using the invisibility-detection procedure and that observed creature's level and intelligence.
bullets: After detecting it, cast at the small disturbance marking the magical view.
Darkness stops the observation for its duration; dispel magic stops it for a day.
